subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Christianity The Person Of Jesus Christ
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The work of the Taizé community is best known for promoting Christian:
options: Prayer, reconciliation and unity among young people
questions.explain: The Taizé community is known for prayer, reconciliation and bringing young Christians of different traditions together.

questions.q: For Christians, the main purpose of pilgrimage is to:
options: Grow spiritually and draw closer to God
questions.explain: Pilgrimage is a spiritual journey undertaken to deepen faith and draw closer to God.

questions.q: For Christians, Easter primarily celebrates:
options: The giving of the Ten Commandments
questions.explain: Easter is the festival celebrating Jesus' resurrection from the dead.

questions.q: Non-liturgical worship typically:
options: Is less formal and may be led freely without a set structure
Requires a bishop to lead it
Always follows a fixed Latin order
questions.explain: Non-liturgical worship is informal and flexible, often found in Free Churches and Pentecostal services.

questions.q: Advent is the period in the Christian year when believers:
options: Prepare for the coming of Jesus at Christmas
questions.explain: Advent is the season of preparation leading up to Christmas and the celebration of Jesus' birth.

questions.q: Infant baptism differs from believers' baptism mainly because it is:
options: Given to babies, with promises made by parents and godparents
questions.explain: Infant baptism is given to babies, with parents and godparents making promises on their behalf.

questions.q: Street Pastors are an example of Christians serving the community by:
options: Offering care and support to people on city streets at night
questions.explain: Street Pastors put faith into action by caring for people in their local community, especially at night.

questions.q: Iona is a place of Christian pilgrimage located in:
questions.explain: Iona is a small Scottish island known for its early Christian community and place of spiritual retreat.

questions.q: At Pentecost, the early Christians received:
questions.explain: At Pentecost the disciples received the Holy Spirit, empowering them to spread Jesus' message.

questions.q: Lent is observed by many Christians as a time of:
options: Fasting, prayer and self-denial before Easter
questions.explain: Lent is a 40-day period of fasting, prayer and reflection that prepares Christians for Easter.

questions.q: Reconciliation between Christian denominations is encouraged by the:
questions.explain: The ecumenical movement works to bring Christian denominations closer together in unity and cooperation.

questions.q: Quaker worship is distinctive because it often involves:
options: Silent waiting on God, with people speaking only when moved to
Elaborate processions led by a bishop
A set order with incense and statues
questions.explain: Quakers typically worship in silence, with individuals speaking only when they feel moved by God.

questions.q: A sacrament in Christianity is understood as:
options: An outward sign of inward grace
questions.explain: A sacrament is an outward, visible sign of an inward, spiritual grace, such as baptism.

questions.q: Christian evangelism is best described as:
options: Spreading the Christian message to others
questions.explain: Evangelism is sharing and spreading the good news of Christianity with others.

questions.q: Private prayer for many Christians involves:
options: Speaking personally to God, sometimes in silence
Always using a priest as a go-between
questions.explain: Private prayer is personal communication with God, which may be spoken or silent.

questions.q: Liturgical worship is best described as worship that:
options: Follows a set structure and order of service
Has no set order and is spontaneous
questions.explain: Liturgical worship follows a set, formal structure, such as in Catholic or Anglican services.

questions.q: In the Roman Catholic Mass, the belief that the bread and wine truly become the body and blood of Christ is called:
questions.explain: Transubstantiation is the Catholic belief that the bread and wine become the actual body and blood of Christ.

questions.q: Lourdes is an important Christian pilgrimage site mainly associated with:
options: Healing and a vision of Mary
questions.explain: Lourdes in France is a Catholic pilgrimage site linked to a vision of Mary and reports of healing.

questions.q: In the Eucharist (Holy Communion), Christians share:
options: Bread and wine in memory of Jesus' Last Supper
questions.explain: The Eucharist uses bread and wine to remember Jesus' sacrifice at the Last Supper.

questions.q: Christmas is the Christian festival that celebrates:
questions.explain: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus, the Incarnation of God as a human.

questions.q: The Lord's Prayer is especially important to Christians because it was:
options: Taught by Jesus to his followers
First used at the Council of Nicaea
questions.explain: Christians value the Lord's Prayer because Jesus himself taught it to his disciples as a model of prayer.

questions.q: The worldwide church works to support people through:
options: Charities and aid such as Christian Aid and CAFOD
questions.explain: The worldwide church supports people globally through charities like Christian Aid and CAFOD.
